involve mandatory fortiﬁcation of foods with folic acid, have been shown to be largely ineffective in reducing NTDs. Mandatory
folic acid-fortiﬁcation of food is proven to be a highly effective measure to prevent NTD, but policy in this area remains controversial
owing to concernsdas yet unprovendrelated to potential adverse effects of over-exposure to folic acid. In the absence of
population-wide fortiﬁcation in many countries, optimizing folate status of mothers in early pregnancy to provide protection
against NTDs remains challenging. This means that, despite the existence of robust scientiﬁc evidence for nearly three decades of
the beneﬁts of folic acid intervention, preventable NTDs are not being prevented in many countries worldwide, including in Europe.
